summary.text: In geology, a rock is any naturally occurring solid mass or aggregate of minerals or mineraloid matter.

Rocks are usually sorted into three main groups by how they form: igneous rock from cooled magma or lava, sedimentary rock from hardened sediment, and metamorphic rock from rock remade by heat and pressure.
Rocks make up Earth's crust and most of its interior, and over time the rock cycle can turn one type of rock into another.

items.prompt: Lava from an undersea eruption cools and hardens on the seabed. Which main group does the new rock belong to?
items.explain: Rock made when magma or lava cools, including lava on the seabed, is igneous.

items.prompt: An existing rock is squeezed and heated so hard that it changes into a new rock, yet it never melts. What kind of rock is it now?
items.explain: Metamorphic rocks form when existing rocks are transformed by high pressure and temperature without significant melting.

items.prompt: Rock makes up Earth's crust and most of its interior. Which part of the inside of the Earth is the big exception?
items.explain: Apart from the liquid outer core and pockets of magma in the asthenosphere, Earth's interior is made of rock.

items.prompt: Roughly how much of Earth's crust, by volume, is made of igneous rock?
items.explain: About 65% of Earth's crust by volume consists of igneous rocks.

items.prompt: As magma rises toward the surface it tends to get richer in silica. What drives this change?

options.label: Air from the surface dissolves into it and adds silica
Low-silica minerals crystallize out and it absorbs silica-rich crust
Rising pressure squeezes silica out of the mantle into it
Groundwater carries dissolved silica in from nearby rock

items.explain: Minerals low in silica crystallize out first as the magma cools, and the magma also takes in crustal rock, which tends to be high in silica.

items.prompt: Sand and mud worn off nearby hills wash into a lake, settle on the bottom, and over a very long time harden into stone. Which group is that stone?
items.explain: Sedimentary rock forms when sediment, produced by weathering, transport and deposition of older rock, is compacted and hardened.
